content.overview: Lighting verification should leave a reconstructable record of what was measured, under which operating state, how the map was calculated, what changed and which next action is supported.

vocabulary.definition: A traceable record of meter, grid, operating state, measured distribution and interpretation.
Relevant condition such as fixture output level, photoperiod phase, canopy height or recent maintenance state.
A repeat measurement used to determine whether an authorized change produced the intended effect.

sections.title: Record the basis of comparison
sections.body: Meter identity, grid, crop plane, fixture output state, canopy condition and timestamp should be preserved so future maps can be compared defensibly.

sections.title: Verify after meaningful change
sections.body: Fixture replacement, height changes, dimming adjustments and major canopy changes should trigger repeat measurement before assuming the new state is equivalent.

sections.title: Keep electrical authority separate
sections.body: A specialist may identify a lighting-distribution problem without being authorized to open fixtures, modify circuits or perform electrical repair. Escalate according to role and procedure.

workedExamples: A map can document a persistent dim edge zone and recommend qualified fixture/layout review without directing unauthorized electrical work.
commonMistakes: Failing to record fixture output or canopy height.
Performing electrical work because the light map is clear.
content.practicalApplication: Write a lighting verification report that includes map method, results, uniformity interpretation, limits, permitted action and escalation owner.
content.summary: A lighting map becomes operational evidence only when its measurement basis and decision boundary are preserved.
